summary: Two towers on Michigan Island in Lake Superior: the 1857 stone light (dark since 1929) and the 1929 iron tower from Schooner Ledge that still shows the light.

events.note: Congress appropriated $5,000 for a light to mark the way to La Pointe

Light commenced operation (LighthouseFriends); Park Service says the lamp was out after about a year
Operations halted; lens sent to La Pointe
Congress provided $6,000 to renovate and relight the station (20 July 1868)

Lightning struck the old tower, 5 May 1889; moderate damage

Board requested $100,000 for a new light and fog signal (repeated annually until 1918)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station record asks whether the light is still lit. The new tower carries the light (LighthouseFriends: a solar-powered LED beacon; the Park Service: automated). The old tower has been dark since 29 Oct 1929 (LighthouseFriends).
The record gives 19.5 m (about 64 ft), matching the archive (64 ft) and LighthouseFriends (65 ft). The Park Service gives 52 ft (about 16 m). Not settled; the story gives both.
LighthouseFriends quotes an 1870 newspaper at 15 miles east of Bayfield; the Park Service says 17 miles northeast.
Records of the Old light's keepers' dwelling and the 1929 dwelling vary between sources; not resolved here.

The Park Service attributes the first tower's 3.5-order lens to Henri Lapaute of Paris. LighthouseFriends gives the 1869 relit lens as third-and-a-half order without naming a maker. The story attributes Paris to the first lens only.

corrections.current: tower, skeletal, stone, built 1857, 36.0 m, standing
corrections.proposed: tower, cast-iron skeletal, built 1880 at Schooner Ledge (Delaware River), moved to Michigan Island and erected 1929; 112 ft (about 34 m); active
corrections.why: The new tower is iron, not stone, and was not built in 1857. The 1857 tower is the stone rubblestone light, which is dark.
The NRHP nomination gives the focal plane of the (new) light as 160 feet (about 48.8 m) above the lake. No source read gives 51.8 m (170 ft).

notes_for_editor: 1) The 1857 'Michigan Island Light' and 1929 tower are both in this one station record. 2) Keepers: the archive roster is the basis; Anna Maria Carlson is in the story as a family member only; she is not a keeper per the archive. 3) Women keepers: Helen L. Pendergrast (first assistant 1872-74) and Matilda Rumrill (first assistant 1874-82) are named in the story with their roles. 4) Lane appears in both the Old and New rosters (1902-1929 and 1929-1939), one line each. 5) Two first-hand sources were not reachable: the 1951 USCG Historical Section report 'History of Michigan Island Light Station' by F. R. Eldridge (listed in the NRHP bibliography) and HABS WI-317 (loc.gov, not called directly). The Lake Carriers' Association 1908 report and the 1867 Board report are known only through LighthouseFriends. 6) The Lighthouse Board reports for 1856-1890 are not in the local corpus; the 1857, 1868-69 and 1889 events rest on LighthouseFriends and the NPS. 7) The 1915-1922 Commissioner volume was used for the 1910 estimate (estimate No. 47, printed p.88, scan p.93). 8) The 1928-1929 cost ($61,041) comes from LighthouseFriends only. 9) The LighthouseFriends DBC-224 spelling vs the NPS DCB-224: story uses DCB-224 per the NPS. 10) Newspapers: not searched for this station (budget); Chronicling America coverage of Wisconsin was not tried. 11) The Carlson ice drift and the Westveld fall are from LighthouseFriends and are not confirmed in the archive's documents. 12) The NRHP nomination is a multi-property nomination; the Michigan Island section was read by --grep. The station's focal plane for the old light is about 124 ft (NRHP); the story does not use it. The new light's focal plane is 160 ft (NRHP). 13) The NPS article gives the 1889 lightning damage as moderate and says copper poles kept the building from being destroyed; LighthouseFriends says the same event caused no serious injury; both are given as each source's view. 14) Lane's 1914 rescue: the Bulletin index entry gives 'Lane, Edward J., keeper Michigan Island, rescue' at p.136; the Bulletin text (PDF p.40) is the source for the quoted facts; the Bulletin says Lane and Pedersen brought the man to the light station. 15) The 1929 lens transfer and the 'log' passage come from LighthouseFriends, which quotes the keeper's log; the original log was not read. 16) Light status, unresolved: LighthouseFriends describes a solar-powered LED beacon in the new tower; the USLHS record for Michigan Island New gives 'Active Aid to Navigation?: No' and 'Current Optic: REMOVED'. The story states both and does not choose. 17) Lighthouse Board and Bulletin items not in the story: the Bulletin records Lane assisting a stranded tug on 20 October 1919 (Bulletin PDF p.44; the 1918-1923 index p.11 and p.24 also list the station), and a later Lane rescue in the 1924-1929 index (p.16). The 1919 Bulletin entry labels the station 'Mich.'; the station is in Wisconsin. Both could be written up. 18) Kirkendall's dates: the USLHS record gives 1933-1937 (used here); LighthouseFriends gives 1933-1936. 19) The NPS gives the 1869 relighting as 16 September; LighthouseFriends gives 15 September. The story says September 1869.
